requirements.requirement: Containerized web application runs as unprivileged appsvc account, serving on port 8080
requirements.summary: appsvc created as uid 1000 non-root user; rootless podman quadlet unit (webapp.container) with PublishPort=8080:80 confirmed running under appsvc's systemd --user instance; podman ps shows container owned by appsvc listening on 0.0.0.0:8080; curl to NODE_IP:8080 returns HTTP 200 with the expected Apache page, both before and after a full node reboot.

requirements.requirement: Service starts at boot while the appsvc account has no active login session
requirements.summary: loginctl enable-linger appsvc set Linger=yes; a bounded reboot was performed with a captured pre-reboot boot_id (6bb7e004...), a reboot acknowledgement, connection loss during the transition, and a distinct post-reboot boot_id (26b9b59d...). After reboot, webapp.service is active, a new container instance auto-started via lingering (4s uptime), HTTP 200 is served on port 8080, loginctl list-sessions reports no sessions, and appsvc processes show TTY '?' (no controlling terminal), directly demonstrating boot-time start without an interactive login both before and after the transition.

overall_summary: The executor deployed a rootless podman container (httpd:alpine) as the unprivileged appsvc user on node1 via a systemd --user quadlet unit, exposed on port 8080, with lingering enabled so it starts at boot without an active login session. Both material outcomes are directly supported by pre- and post-reboot evidence: a full node reboot was performed and observed (distinct boot IDs, brief unreachability, then recovery), after which the service, container, and port-8080 HTTP response were all confirmed healthy while loginctl reported zero sessions and appsvc processes had no controlling TTY. The lifecycle snapshots corroborate the boot-identity change and the addition of the expected 8080 listening socket with no failed services. Hygiene is clean aside from a few small residual log files in /tmp.
limitations: The reboot verification window is short (a few seconds of unreachability); a longer-duration or repeated reboot was not performed to further confirm persistence across multiple boots.
Evidence relies on curl/loginctl/systemctl output captured by the executor rather than an independent verifier probe, though these are direct command observations rather than executor self-report.

operational_hygiene.summary: All executor commands map clearly to installing podman, creating the appsvc user, configuring lingering, writing the quadlet unit, starting/verifying the service, and performing the mandatory reboot verification — no unnecessary or unexplained mutations were found. The only residue is a handful of small log/pid files left in /tmp (podman_install.log, reboot.log, start.log, start.pid), which are low-risk, non-conflicting artifacts of legitimate installation/verification steps rather than abandoned experiments or unsafe exposure. No failed or conflicting services were introduced (failed-services list remains empty after execution) and no package-health regression is evident.
